title: Sistema Borges - James G. Coke IV, 2010
credits: Sistema Borges, Rancho Borges, Tulum, Quintana Roo, Mexico; length 319.9 m, depth -4.5 m; surveyed with Suunto, clinometer, tape and Disto A3, February 2010, by James G. Coke IV; drawn by James G. Coke IV, April 2010. (c) 2010 James G. Coke IV (AMCS Activities Newsletter 33, p. 62, 2010)
sistemaWhy: Sistema created in the local database at the user's request (2026-10-02) from this map: Borges. No Sistema Borges in the database (nor any cave named Borges): sistemaId left empty for the user to create it. Its sump leads to 'Cenote Garza (Cueva Inundada)': the database's only Garza (-KPZkVJm0TntehY0DgPo, Gerrard 2015, no position) is filed under Swan Lake Spring (-KPZgfyGw3nChUfwqTYa, 1257.9 m, 14.9 m, 'located 650 m southeast of Sistema Dos Pisos') - perhaps the flooded cave meant here, but nothing on the map confirms it.
unverified: No cenote of the map has a position: Sistema Borges and Rancho Borges are in neither the database nor OpenStreetMap (OSM's only 'Borges' near Tulum is a restaurant on Avenida Tulum), and the database's Garza has no position. The map is put, by its scale bar and north, with its Garza sump on a guessed spot for Swan Lake Spring (650 m south-east of Dos Pisos' position, from Gerrard's direction) - a guess only, which falls among houses and canopy.
wetDry: Shallow water cave, kept by the user's decision: the pale blue fill ('Agua' in the legend) covers most of the passages, 1.0-2.0 m deep (blue overlined numbers), under 1.2-2.9 m of ceiling (circled); the rest is mud, sand and breakdown floor around the entrance collapse. The west end sumps ('Sifon a Cenote Garza (Cueva Inundada)'), the way on to the flooded cave.
northWhy: The arrow is magnetic north 2006 with a declination of 0 deg 02' E (as on Coke's Tixik K'una map of 2008): north is up. Nothing on the ground could check it.
placementWhy: Scale bar (0-45 m, 1227 px: 0.0367 m/px; the cross-sections' 6 m bars, 'at the map's scale', agree within 1%) and north (magnetic 2006, 0 deg 02' E: up), shifted so the sump to Cenote Garza (west end) lands on a guessed position for the database's Swan Lake Spring: 650 m south-east of Sistema Dos Pisos (20.18979, -87.54207), from Gerrard's direction. Unchecked: no point of the map has a known position (see unverified); the nearest placed map is Ox Bel Ha 2011, 600 m away, which doesn't overlap.

entrances.name: Entrada Sistema Borges
entrances.why: the open collapse at the east end (boulders and plants inside the ticked 'Limite de cueva' line), the map's datum (Ø Datum); not in the database

detailLines.why: skylight (spoked ring with a plant) in the mud east of 4.1: a roof opening, not a pillar

symbols.why: Coke's legend: overlined numbers are depths - black ones the floor depth below the datum (profundidad del piso: 4.1, 4.5, 4.5), blue ones the water's depth (profundidad del agua, 1.0-2.0) - both typed depth, as on Tixik K'una; circled ones ceiling heights; tb low ceiling. Checked by eye against the map: 14 depths, 12 ceiling heights, 1 tb; OCR missed the 1.7 (once masked by the top section's box, now cut back) and the circled 2.7 (in extra). No bones (no legend icon, none drawn, no word), no flow arrows, no '?': the small bent arrows beside the passages are the cross-sections' marks. The spoked rings with a plant (east of 4.1, and two in the sand south of it) are skylights, not typed. The dashed lines at tb are 'pasaje sin topografia' (unsurveyed passage), left as drawn.
